brief.situation: 11:00 at Mrs. Albright's home. You are the home health physical therapist. She is 86, three weeks after a hip fracture repair. Her daughter says she has been 'sleepy and off' since yesterday and 'just tired from the therapy'.
handover: She has a urinary catheter that was removed 5 days ago and has been going to the toilet often since.
Agency policy: hold therapy and call 911 for signs of sepsis or acute illness; notify the provider.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Why is Mrs. Albright sleepy and off today, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: New drowsiness and inattention are hypoactive delirium, the form most often missed; with fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, a low pressure and urinary symptoms, sepsis (likely urinary) needs emergency care.
parts.modelAnswer: This isn't tiredness. She's got hypoactive delirium, the quiet kind people miss, plus a fever, fast heart rate and breathing, low pressure and urinary symptoms. That's sepsis.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Holds therapy, calls 911 and her provider, explains to her daughter and documents.
parts.modelAnswer: No therapy today, call 911 and her provider, explain to her daughter and document.

scoring.modelReasoning: Physical therapists must recognize conditions needing medical referral, including sepsis, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance and acute cardiac events. Delirium is an acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness; the quiet hypoactive form is the one most often missed and is often the first sign of infection in an older adult. Mrs. Albright's fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, low pressure and urinary symptoms point to urinary sepsis: hold therapy and call 911.
